title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.91). S is a scheme of finite type over a field such as Q, assumed normal and probably regular, with function field K. X -> S is a relative smooth proper curve and U ⊂ X is the complement of a relative divisor at infinity, so U is a relative affine curve. E_• denotes arithmetic fundamental groups (Galois groups). ξ is a section of E_{U_K} -> E_K, i.e. a Galois section for the generic fibre. The problem is to 'specialize' ξ to sections of E_{X_s} -> E_{k(s)} at points s of S. This is a sections-conjecture analogue of extending a K-rational point of U_K to a rational section of X over S.

Setup from p.91. Let S~ be the normalization of S in K̄ (on p.91 this is called S'). The fibre over s is the set of maximal ideals of the normal closure of O_{S,s} in K̄. For s' in that fibre, N_{s'} is the decomposition group (stabilizer) in E_K. There is an extension 1 -> I_{s'} -> N_{s'} -> E_{k(s)} -> 1.

This page.
- I_{s'} ≅ E_{K~}, where K~ is the fraction field of the strict henselization of O_{S,s'}.
- N_{s'} ≅ E of the fraction field of the non-strict henselization.
- Suppose the composite E_K -> E_{U_K} -> E_U kills I_{s'}; equivalently its image in the geometric π kills I_{s'}. Grothendieck now writes 's' ∈ S'', so S' has become the 'good' (unramified) locus. Then, as in the codimension-1 case, the restriction to N_{s'} induces a homomorphism E_{k(s)} -> E_U.
- This factors through E_{k(s)} -> E_{U_{Õ_s}} ≅ E_{X_s}, via the specialization isomorphism for the henselized family. So it is a section of E_{X_s} over E_{k(s)}.

Then: what happens for s ∉ S'?
- D = S \ S' is purely of codimension 1. Grothendieck glosses D as the image under f of the divisors T on X along which the (rational) section meets infinity with multiplicity j ≥ 1. The analogy is with a rational point: by the valuative criterion it is defined off codim ≥2, and it fails to land in U along a divisor.
- One then considers the μ = μ_d (Kummer, tame) torsor structure attached to a component D_α. The next page states that the integer d is the multiplicity of the section along D_α.
- At the generic point s_α of D_α, the specialized object is no longer a section into the open curve. It is a cuspidal ('point at infinity') section: a cusp i_α ∈ X_{s_α} \ U_{s_α}, rational over k(s_α), together with its canonical inertia subgroup L_i ≅ Ẑ(1) in π. The inertia I_{s_α} ≅ Ẑ(1) maps into it by multiplication by the multiplicity.

In short, the page outlines a theory of specialization of Galois sections over a higher-dimensional base: a good locus, a ramification divisor D, and cuspidal degeneration along D with an inertia degree equal to the intersection multiplicity.
errors: Notation clash: on p.91 S' is the normalization of S in K̄ (with points s'), while on this page S' denotes the open 'unramified' locus where the inertia I_{s'} is killed ('ce qui signifie justement s' ∈ S''). In the D = S \ S' statement S' is the good locus in S.

The claim that D = S \ S' is purely of codimension 1 is clear for genuine rational points (valuative criterion, Weil extension) or for each finite quotient by Zariski–Nagata purity on regular S. For an arbitrary Galois section, the ramification locus is a priori an increasing union over finite quotients of pure-codim-1 closed sets. Such a union need not be closed or finite without extra input (e.g. the section conjecture itself, or a finiteness argument). Grothendieck's gloss via 'diviseurs T sur X' implicitly assumes the section comes from a rational point (or quasi-section).
Regularity of S is needed for purity but is not stated on this page; only normality is used for the normalization.

ideas.what: Specialization of a Galois section of π1(U_K) -> G_K to sections of π1(X_s) -> G_{k(s)} at points where the inertia is killed, using decomposition/inertia groups in the normalization of S in K̄ and the henselian specialization isomorphism.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of sections (good reduction locus) in the section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stix (specialization of sections, LNM 2054 'Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups', 2013); earlier implicit in Nakamura, Tamagawa
ideas.where_published: Hinted at only generally in the 1983 letter to Faltings; not worked out there

ideas.what: Bad locus D = S \ S' is pure codimension 1, analogous to the indeterminacy locus of a rational point landing at infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Zariski–Nagata purity applied to ramification of sections

ideas.what: Along a component D_α the section degenerates to a cuspidal section; the inertia map Ẑ(1) -> cuspidal inertia is multiplication by the intersection multiplicity d (μ_d-torsor).
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal sections / tangential base points; degree of the inertia map equals contact multiplicity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989), Ihara–Nakamura, Nakamura; Stix (cuspidal sections)
ideas.where_published: Cuspidal 'packets' of sections mentioned in the 1983 letter to Faltings; no detailed statement known

missed.claim: A relative/higher-dimensional specialization theory for Galois sections over a base S of arbitrary dimension: a good open locus, a pure-codim-1 ramification divisor, and generic cuspidal degeneration with multiplicities. This is sketched as a Galois-theoretic analogue of the valuative criterion. The literature mostly treats specialization over DVRs or curves.
missed.quote: Et que se passe-t-il pour s ∉ S' ? ... D = S \ S' est purement de codim 1 ... on fait le μ = μ_d ... relatif à une composante D_α
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A purity theorem for the ramification locus of an arbitrary Galois section, for families over a higher-dimensional base, is not standard. It would be an anabelian analogue of Weil's extension theorem and is relevant to the section conjecture over function fields of higher transcendence degree.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent early (c.1981) sketch of section specialization and cuspidal degeneration with multiplicities, before Deligne/Nakamura/Stix. However, the individual ingredients are now known, and the codim-1 purity for genuine sections is asserted without proof.
transcription_corrections: '$\mathcal{E}_{K(s)}$' should be '$\mathcal{E}_{k(s)}$' (residue field) in both occurrences.
'on sait factorise par' is likely 'on voit qu'il se factorise par'.
'(ce qui signifie justement s' ∈ S' ...)' : S' here denotes the good locus, not the normalization.
'hensélisé (strict) de O_{S,s'}' : the parenthetical gives N_{s'} ≅ E_{K~} with K~ the fraction field of the non-strict henselization.
'Bon[?]. On. on peut[?]' is probably 'Bon. On sait que' or 'Rappelons que'.
'la fonction f de X sur S' may be 'la section f de X sur S' (rational section).
